summary: A weekly, donation-based meditation and restorative-silence gathering held at Quietude/The Lodge at Quietude in Black Mountain, NC, explicitly framed as a peer respite circle for community care professionals: psychotherapists, social workers, bodyworkers, and spiritual teachers/healers. It targets a specific shared professional identity rather than the general public, and the consistent weekly cadence at the same venue with tags like 'Healers Circle,' 'Peer Support Circle,' and 'Support Groups' suggests a returning core of practitioners rather than a rotating audience, though no named facilitator or independent group page was found to confirm a fixed membership.

evidence.note: Description explicitly targets 'psychotherapists, spiritual teachers, bodyworkers, social workers and more' rather than the general public, framing it as a space for peers in caregiving professions.
The Lodge at Quietude variant is described as offering 'respite, peer connection, and emotional renewal' for clinicians and healers, i.e. peer-support language, not a commercial class.

Both units recur weekly at the same address (1130 Montreat Rd) for months (16 and 7 occurrences respectively) with tags including 'Peer Support Circle', 'Healers Circle', 'Support Groups', and 'For Community Healers', consistent with an ongoing practitioner cohort rather than a one-off class.

Quietude is a general-purpose micro-retreat/event venue in Black Mountain hosting many unrelated workshops and retreats; its own site has no page dedicated to 'Meditation for Community Healers', so this looks like a program renting/using the space rather than a Quietude-branded offering.

Web searches for the event name plus Black Mountain/Asheville and for 'community healers meditation circle facilitator' surfaced no dedicated website, Facebook group, Meetup page, or named facilitator for this specific series.
